Who we are Where we work Questions

The team behind the videos

Vertens Ad Studio is the short-video team of the Sunvega Group. We do overseas social media marketing, and what we are best at is marketing for physical stores abroad — the restaurants, salons, showrooms and garages that live on people walking through the door.

Part of Sunvega Group

We are the short-video team inside Sunvega Group, working alongside its overseas marketing and supply-chain businesses.

Overseas social media

TikTok, Instagram, Facebook, YouTube Shorts — writing, editing and running paid campaigns in five languages.

Storefronts, above all

Our work is built around local stores overseas: what makes someone in the neighbourhood put down the phone and come in.

How we work

We film nothing ourselves. You shoot on a phone with our shot list, our editors write and cut, and one 30-minute session becomes a month of videos. That is the whole reason a month costs a few hundred dollars instead of a few thousand.

Where we can work

We send no crew, so we can work anywhere you can film on a phone. These are the areas we are set up for — the trades listed under each are the ones we already have scripts and sample libraries for.

Your city not on the list? It changes nothing about how we work — tell us where you are and we start the same way.

Questions store owners ask us

Short video ads for local stores — what it costs, how it is made, and what you have to do. If your question is not here, message us on WhatsApp.

Getting started

How much does a short video ad cost for a small store?

A Basic month is $449 for eight videos — three 30-second and five 15-second — which works out to about $56 a video. Standard is $799 for fifteen videos, about $53 each. Scripts, filming plan, editing and captions are included. There is no setup fee and no contract.

Can I see something before I pay?

Yes, two things, both free. Paste your page link and we send a read of your page plus ten scripts written for your trade. After that we make one full 15-second video from your own footage, also free. You only pay if you want more.

I don't have any videos of my store. Can you still help?

Yes. Photos are enough to start. If you want the most real version, we get on a 20-minute video call and tell your staff exactly what to film — one session gives us enough for a whole month of videos.

How long until my first video?

Three business days from the moment your material is complete. The rest of the month's videos follow within about a week.

How the videos are made

Do you send a camera crew to my store?

No, and that is why this costs a few hundred dollars instead of a few thousand. You film on your phone with our shot list; we write, cut, caption and deliver. Nobody has to close the store for a shoot day.

Is this AI video? Will my customers be able to tell?

We use AI, and we tell you exactly where. In the most common version your store and your face are real footage and only the voice and lip-sync are AI. Food, faces and materials always come from real footage, because AI versions of those look fake to anyone who knows the trade.

How do you get fifteen videos out of one filming session?

One 30-minute session gives us the raw pieces — you at the door, you inside, you holding the product, plus detail shots and photos. Fifteen scripts recombine those pieces differently, each with its own hook and ending. That is enough to post every other day for a month.

What if I don't like the first video?

We redo it until it is right, or you get your money back. You also keep the raw footage either way — it is your store and your material.

Ads and results

Can you also run the ads, not just make the videos?

Yes, it is a separate order. You pay us the ad spend plus $100 a month for account management, plus 10% of the first $5,000 of spend and 5% of anything above that. Most stores start at $500 a month. We build the campaigns, watch them daily and report spend and leads weekly.

What aspect ratio do I get, and where do these run?

Everything is delivered vertical, 9:16 only — that is the shape TikTok and Facebook were built around, and the only one people watch full-screen on a phone. The same 15- and 30-second files work as organic posts and as Meta and TikTok ad creatives. We do not export square or landscape versions.

Can the videos be in Chinese, Spanish, Vietnamese or Korean?

Yes. We write and caption in English, Chinese, Spanish, Vietnamese and Korean, and most stores run two languages side by side — one for the neighbourhood and one for everyone else.

Where we work

Do you work with stores in my city?

We work wherever your phone does, because nobody flies out to film. Most of our stores are in Los Angeles, Irvine, Rowland Heights, San Gabriel, Flushing, Houston, Toronto, Vancouver and Sydney, and the process is identical anywhere else.

Which kinds of stores is this for?

Restaurants and cafés, beauty and nail salons, building materials and furniture showrooms, and auto services — the trades where someone has to walk in the door. We keep ten sample scripts ready for each.

I have several locations. Does that change anything?

Yes, in your favour. One filming session can cover shared product and brand shots, and only the storefront and staff lines change per location. Tell us how many stores you have and we price it as one plan.

Working with us

Do I have to sign a contract?

No. Videos are ordered by the month and you can stop after any month. Ad management is also monthly and can be stopped any time.

Who owns the videos?

You do. Finished videos, raw footage and scripts are yours to use anywhere, including on channels we do not run for you.

How do I actually start?

Paste your page link and leave your WhatsApp. Within one business day an editor sends the page read and ten scripts. If they look right, we make the free sample next.

Still deciding? The quickest way to see what we would do with your store is ten free scripts — one business day, no account.

So why is a video $53 and not $500?

Because none of these three ways spends money on the expensive part of video. Here is exactly where the cost went.

01
Nobody drives to your store

A videographer on site costs $500–1,500 a day, before anyone edits anything. We never send one. The phone already in your pocket is the camera, and the shot list tells your staff exactly what to point it at.

02
One filming session, ten videos

The same 90 minutes of footage becomes ten different ads — new hook, new length, new language, new offer. Traditional production reshoots for every version. We reshoot for none.

03
AI does the repeating, not the acting

Voice, lip-sync, captions, resizing, twenty variations — that is machine work and it costs almost nothing. Your face and your store stay real, which is the part that actually sells.

Agency video: $500+ each· UGC marketplaces: $99–167 each· Us: about $53 Same real footage. We just stopped paying for the parts that don't show up on screen.
